sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The old Celtic religion left a part in later folk tales. The magic of the faith turned toward gain in the tales. Leprechauns came to be sought for the gold at their pot. The treasure of a goddess turned into a spot called the Money Hole, one place in the mountain that gave wealth on one's bare hand. In places a thistle rises where the gold of a fairy lies below. A thing of the old rites slid into a search for the purse.

okr.objective: Religion’s old magic changed into a search for the gold in Irish folk tales.
key_results: Old magic set a price in later tales.
